### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/vitest.repo-tests.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/vitest.repo-tests.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`, `/meta/:type/:name (route, 45 pages)`
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `69d6ee46319907fc30ff36c8f0a99c0b01e576d2` — the merge of head `ee2468e8fe5863e98a14c1f68253576eb265e35a` into base `7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 69d6ee46319907fc30ff36c8f0a99c0b01e576d2 && git checkout 69d6ee46319907fc30ff36c8f0a99c0b01e576d2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b ee2468e8fe5863e98a14c1f68253576eb265e35a && git checkout -B drift-repro 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b && git merge --no-ff ee2468e8fe5863e98a14c1f68253576eb265e35a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7ac04795da3bf4101eaea30811997dcc8d7d4d4b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e12cc9ba0a8019b75567930b0244fa48f0e184ca`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/record-currency-path.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json

Code outside the diff was read to judge the scope files, not reviewed: `engine-registration.ts`, `plugin.ts` (objectql), `protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, `validation/record-currency-code.ts`, `rest/meta-item-write-routes.ts`, `runtime/domains/meta.ts`, `spec/api/protocol.zod.ts`. The rest of the diff (tests, docs, changeset body) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. Completed green include Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates. No gate verdict on tests, build or type check exists yet for this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Doors that now refuse and admitted before: declared right, with two undeclared changes.** Right as declared: `SchemaRegistry.registerObject` on a sealed registry (every direct caller), and a published `/meta` single save on `meta-envelope` or `meta-dispatch`, which now asks D6's door and the follow door before anything is stored. Wrong, because undeclared: (1) a declaration `defineStack` admits and the cold boot registers is refused at a post-seal `registerApp` (finding F1); (2) the per-item publish of a draft now ends `published` with the object unregistered (finding F2).
- **Drafts, batch faces, package install, artifact load.** A draft save is unchanged (body-only). The batch `saveMetaItem` faces keep the body-only pre-flight, but their outcome is not what it was on `main`: a bad follow pair was stored and registered there, and is now stored and left unregistered with a `console.warn`. The PR body's table states that outcome. Package install and artifact load after the seal do not keep their path: `registerApp` throws on a follow refusal (the PR body says so), and it also throws on a valid package (F1). This contradicts the ruling line "Batch saves, package install and artifact load keep their current path."
- **Can a boot that succeeds on `main` fail or lose an object: no, for the cold boot.** The follow door and the `againstRegistry` option are both gated on `bareNameHoldersAreSealed`, set in objectql's `kernel:bootstrapped` handler; artifact bodies, manifest `objectExtensions` and `sys_metadata` rows register before it. D6's door is untouched in the boot. Not verified exhaustively: handlers of other plugins on `kernel:bootstrapped` or `kernel:listening` that run after the seal; none was found registering an object with a currency path.
- **Post-seal gate.** A pair registered before the seal with a bad follow is never judged until one end registers again; every restart re-admits it. That is the ruled deviation and is stated. When a parent re-registers later, the pair is judged there (the "other ends" loop), as D6 does. Consequence, declared in Clause-②: with a bad pair already registered, every later save of the parent is refused until the child or the parent's code field is fixed, including a save that changes something else.
- **One builder, no copied strings: right.** The (a) messages, the (c) head and the unfollowed reason exist once, in `record-currency-path.ts`; the stack check and the registry door both call them. The registry door adds one prefix sentence of its own for the parent end.
- **`collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` after the move: unchanged.** Compared arm by arm: `isRecord` and `hasOwnKey` have the same semantics in both files, the code-field predicate is the same expression, the two (a) messages and the (c) head are the same text, the `judgeRecord` condition and the `continue` paths are untouched, and `refuseRecord` still serves the arms that did not move. No condition changed.
- **New spec export: not a schema or authorable-key move.** Four functions and two interfaces from `@objectstack/spec/data`; no Zod schema and no key is added, removed or re-shaped. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly those six entries and agree with the source.
- **`writeFace` is now an accept-set predicate.** Before this diff it only chose how a refusal is rendered. Its published description (`SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.writeFace`, `protocol.zod.ts`, outside the diff) still says "Two refusals branch on it". See ④.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, each `patch`. These are the three released packages the diff moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md rule 3). Level and packages are right.
- Declaration lines: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present in the PR body and the changeset, and match the corrected claim.
- Narrowing obligations: `!` in the PR title, present. BREAKING banner in the changeset, present. **BREAKING banner in the PR body, absent** (the word does not occur in the body); a prose-face fix, nit N1. ADR-0087 marker, exactly one (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and its reason holds: no key moves and a stored row boots as before. `Skills-docs:` line, present in the PR body.
- Dogfood battery: os-dev-report 6782303275 records it on `e12cc9ba`, the reviewed head (450 files passed, 3 skipped; 3757 tests passed, 42 skipped; lock verdict exit 0).
- The Clause-② sentence under-states what the tree narrows (F1) and what it leaves silent (F2). It needs restating once those are fixed or ruled.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: one, the batch `saveMetaItem` writers that store an object the registry refuses and only warn. Answered: filed as #32369 by the seat. The PR body still says "a follow-up card is drafted"; it should name #32369 (prose).
- **Is the PR body honest about the batch faces: partly.** The table gives the measured outcome for the four `saveMetaItem` batch faces. Three things are wrong or missing:
  - It says the silent store-and-warn "predates this PR for D6". True for D6. For the follow door it is new with this PR: on `main` those rows registered.
  - The publish doors are not in the table: the per-item publish (`POST /meta/object/:name/publish`) and `publishPackageDrafts`. The body says a draft is "registered later, inside the publish batch". The code says otherwise: `promoteDraftForPublish` serves the per-item publish too, which has no sibling.
  - "The boot and an artifact load register exactly what they did on main" holds only before the seal. After it, a reload or a runtime install goes through `registerApp` and is judged.
- #32369 covers the batch `saveMetaItem` faces only. It does not cover the per-item publish, `publishPackageDrafts`, or the post-seal `registerApp` order (F1, F2).
- Escalated to the seat: F1 and F2 each need a fix or a ruling; neither is covered by ruling 6780473954.
- Security: no finding.

### ④ Design judgment

The direction is right. ADR-0144 D2 (amended) requires segment 2 to name a code field on the `master_detail` target, and the object door's jsdoc already assigned that to the registry. Asking the full registry question at a single published save is right, and so is keeping #29673's body-only question where a sibling can still change the pair. Two places in the tree break it.

**`hits` files**

- `packages/spec/src/data/record-currency-path.ts`: holds. Messages and one predicate, no door logic, same words as before the move. The first branch of `unfollowedAmountReason` (a child amount with its own code field) is reached only from the stack check; the registry leaves that arm to D6. No finding.
- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: holds. Behaviour-preserving refactor (see ①). No finding.
- `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`: holds. One `export *`, beside the `controlled-by-parent-master` precedent.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: jsdoc only. It now says the registry judges segment 2 "at a registration after the cold boot", which is true of the tree.
- `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `export-origins/data.json`: agree with the source.

**Implementing files**

- **F1, must-fix. `registry.ts` (the call site and its gate) with `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`: after the seal, the follow door refuses a valid declaration because of registration order.** The PR gates the door on the seal for a stated reason: a package's `objectExtensions` register after its `objects` (`engine-registration.ts`, step 2 then 2b), so a child judged before the extension that adds its parent's code field is refused by a verdict the same run then contradicts. That order does not end at the seal. `registerPackageBody` runs the same two steps on every post-seal `registerApp`: a runtime install through the `manifest` service, and a reload (`refreshReloadedPackages`).
  - Case: package P declares a child whose amount follows `PARENT.p_currency`, where PARENT belongs to an installed package and P's own `objectExtensions` adds `p_currency` as an ISO 4217 code field. `defineStack` admits P (a parent known only through an extension is skipped). The cold boot registers P. A first install of P on a sealed kernel refuses the child at step 2, before step 2b registers the extension, and `restoringOnRefusal` aborts the install. On `main` the install succeeds.
  - The same order reaches the batch writers: a child object row written before the `object_extension` row that completes it is refused at its write-through, warned, and left unregistered until a restart.
  - Why must-fix: it refuses a member of the accept set that the PR does not declare as narrowed, the PR's own rationale names the hazard, and ruling 6780473954 says package install and artifact load keep their path. No pin covers a post-seal `registerApp` with an extension-supplied code field (pin 7 registers the extension first).
  - A fix judges the pair once the registering unit is complete (for `registerApp`, after step 2b and inside the same restore run), or keeps the follow door out of multi-registration units as it is kept out of the boot.
- **F2, must-fix. `protocol-save.ts` (the predicate): the per-item publish is a single-object door left on the batch path, and it now fails silently.** The single-save test is `mode === 'publish'` with face `meta-envelope` or `meta-dispatch`. A draft saved through the same doors is body-only, which is right while it is a draft. Its promotion is not: `promoteDraftForPublish` (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, outside the diff) asks `objectRegistrationRefusal` with no option, and its comment says both the per-item publish and `publishPackageDrafts` reach it.
  - Result on a sealed kernel on this head, by reading: a draft child with a bad path saves `200`; `POST /meta/object/:name/publish` passes the body-only pre-flight, promotes the row, and the write-through `registerObject` throws into `applyObjectRegistryMutation`'s `console.warn`. The publish answers `published`. A new object is not registered; a re-published one keeps its old definition while the store holds the new one.
  - On `main` that object registered, and each amount write was refused loudly. Ruling 6780473954 names exactly this swap ("a loud failure ... for a silent one") as the reason the registry door could not land alone, and #29673's stated rule is that publish tells the truth. The draft-then-publish route is the one #29673 measured Studio using.
  - The per-item publish has no sibling, so #29673's batch reason does not apply to it. `publishPackageDrafts` is a real batch and belongs with #32369.
  - A fix passes `againstRegistry` from the per-item publish (not from the package publish), with a live pin beside the `PUT` ones, and adds both publish doors to the PR body's table.
- **F3, should-fix. `registry.ts`, `extensionFieldsOf`: the two ends of the pair read different parents.** The parent end builds the parent's fields from every `extend` contributor, including those of a disabled package. The child end reads `getObject`, whose fold withholds a disabled package's extensions (`withholdDisabledExtensions`). So a parent re-save is admitted on a code field the served parent does not have, and the child's own save is then refused against the same registry. The error is on the admitting side (the behaviour of `main`), so it is not a must-fix. The view should fold as `resolveObject` does.
- **F4, should-fix. `protocol-save.ts`: the predicate's default is the silent path.** A caller that states no face, or a face added later, gets the body-only question and the store-and-warn outcome. F2 is one instance. The safer shape is for the batch callers to say they are batches, or for the single-row doors to be enumerated in one place with a pin that fails when a new producer of `saveMetaItem` or of the promotion appears. The reverse error was not found: no batch producer sends `meta-envelope` or `meta-dispatch` (each is set at one single-row call site, `rest/meta-item-write-routes.ts` and `runtime/domains/meta.ts`, field by field).
- `protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts`, `protocol.ts`: pass-through of the option; both agree with the registry's signature. The option is honoured only on a sealed registry, decided in the registry, so a caller cannot turn it on during the boot. No finding.
- `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`, the rest of the door, against the probes:
  - parent is the same object (self `master_detail`), and a self roll-up: judged against the incoming body. Right.
  - parent known only through `objectExtensions`: `getObject` returns nothing for an ownerless object, so no verdict. Matches `defineStack`.
  - path whose first segment is a `lookup`: `recordCurrencyPathOf` yields no master, so no verdict here; the spec object door refuses it at the save's parse. Right for a parsed body; a body that skips the parse gets no verdict, as on `main`.
  - an `extend` body: only its own roll-ups are judged. A following amount added by an extension is never judged at the registry. Consistent with what the PR states; not a regression.
  - (c) leaves own-currency and other-relation amounts to D6. Agrees with D6 as amended.

**Nits** (no effect on correctness or the contract)

- N1. PR body carries no BREAKING banner (②). Prose face.
- N2. PR body says the follow-up card is "drafted"; it is #32369. Prose face.
- N3. `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.writeFace`'s description still says the face only selects how refusals are rendered. Follow-up card, since the file is outside this diff.
- N4. The parent-end prefix "'PARENT' would no longer hold the code a registered amount follows" is untrue when the parent never held it (a pair registered during the boot, or a parent registering for the first time after its child). Accepted deviation or follow-up; a code change moves the head.
- N5. The follow door walks every field of every registered object on each sealed registration, and twice on a `/meta` single save (pre-flight, then registration). D6's scan runs only when the body holds a record-mode amount. Post-seal only, so the boot is unaffected. Follow-up.

F1 and F2 are must-fix: FAIL. Their fixes move the head and earn a delta review; F3 and F4 are in the same delta.
